opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
Mercy and Justice

Nineveh was the powerful and violent capital of Assyria. In the time of Jonah, God warned the city of coming judgment, but when the people repented, He showed them mercy and spared them. Generations later, Nineveh had returned to violence, cruelty, and oppression. Through the prophet Nahum, God declared that He would no longer allow it to continue.

Together, Jonah and Nahum reveal something profound about God: His mercy is not weakness, and His justice is not cruelty. God desires repentance and restoration, but His mercy should never be mistaken for indifference toward evil.

This is the heart of redemption: God loves us too much to discard us because of our sin, and He loves us too much to leave us unchanged by it. His mercy calls us back. His justice calls us to change. And through Christ, He offers salvation to us all.
